CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys for syndromic condition.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week-old twin presenting for nephrology evaluation due to Smith-Magenis syndrome. Patient was born weighing 4 pounds 8 ounces. She had neonatal feeding difficulties with apneic episodes during feeding and temperature regulation issues. She has severe gastroesophageal reflux disease and was taken off cow's milk per dietician recommendation. She did not sit by herself or walk by age one year but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She has 8-10 wet diapers per 24-hour period. She drinks pea protein milk, water, and occasionally water with small amounts of juice. She is currently in feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and will be starting speech therapy within the next couple of weeks. She has also been evaluated by orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. The family was informed by geneticist that Smith-Magenis syndrome can be associated with kidney fusion and lower extremity problems. Twin sister is healthy and developing normally, running around without problems, similar size to patient.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for gastroesophageal reflux disease. Negative for abnormal urinary output. Not otherwise discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis syndrome. Neonatal feeding difficulties with apneic episodes. Temperature regulation issues in infancy. Severe gastroesophageal reflux disease. Failure to meet developmental milestones (sitting and walking) by one year of age.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother age 9 with autism. Twin sister without known medical conditions. No family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or transplantation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Family lives in Dallas, Georgia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs examined without abnormality noted. Ears examined.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week-old twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in literature with this chromosomal deletion syndrome. Kidney ultrasound to be obtained today for screening. If abnormalities identified on ultrasound, next steps and future follow-up will be determined. If ultrasound is normal, no further follow-up needed. Follow-up location will be at town center in Dallas area if needed.
